rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: resolving M6's mood early would steal the leverage landing. Strategy doc names M6 mood as unleashed leverage (line 362) and the module's maintainer block names the same target (line 81); the body makes the walk-away window and return-to-notes mechanism explicit (lines 27, 43, 52), then closes on an inspectable loop rather than trust in the agent (line 74).

M6's strategy mood is unleashed leverage, not unease: the strategy arc explicitly places unease in M3/M4 and leverage in M6 (lines 359-362), so this rule's unease-versus-shame condition does not fire on this module.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a failure-led frame would make the module about defects or shame instead of a positive operating discipline. The Big Idea leads with a fixed judge, repeated improvement and a sharper generator (line 4); Key Concepts lead with infrastructure, role separation, walk-away autonomy, a stable yardstick and loop ownership (lines 57-61). The What You'll Learn verbs are Build, Read, Create and Distinguish (lines 12-15), with no failure-mode title or lead.

Harm: front-running a later teaching moment spends its strategic reveal before the student reaches it. The body follows the M6 sequence in the strategy doc: the M5 judge is carried forward, the fixed-judge loop runs for three rounds with separate generation/judging and a walk-away return (lines 23-43; strategy lines 495-507), and the M7 handoff is a forward pointer after the M6 work (lines 63-69), not a premature sharing lesson. The closing human-role framing also matches the strategy's M1-M6 core close (lines 73-74; strategy lines 507-509).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategic themes recur in Key Concepts
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: tactics without worldview leave the student with a procedure but not the strategic reason to reuse it. The five Key Concepts contain clear M6 instances of Compound/Sharpen in 'the work gets sharper' through repeated tactic rewrites (line 60), Ground in holding the judge still as the comparison yardstick (line 60), and agentic autonomy in 'the system runs; you come back to the notes' (line 59); this exceeds the required 2-3 module-specific theme instances without naming a detached theme list.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Key Concepts shape — theme breadcrumbs, not standalone section
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: labelled or repetitive breadcrumbs would turn emergent concepts into trainer-bait and weaken the memorable strategic hooks. The section is a single emergent Key Concepts list (lines 56-61), with no standalone themes section, no Remember label and no breadcrumb wrapper; its compact landing clauses include 'you come back to the notes' (line 59), 'A yardstick you rewrite is not a yardstick' (line 60), and 'quality discipline instead of a content discipline' (line 61). The bullets survive the §3/§4/§5 gates and do not front-run M7's sharing work.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: What You'll Learn shape — capability register, not syllabus
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: syllabus-shaped bullets describe what the curriculum does rather than a capability the participant can use. Each bullet leads with a concrete capability verb plus an immediate object (Build a loop, Read tactic changes, Create eval infrastructure, Distinguish judge shapes; lines 12-15). There are no Bloom tags, author-defence asides or didactic taxonomy stamps; the operational detail names the resulting artifacts and fixed-judge behavior, consistent with the strategy's M6 capability and canonical fixed-judge pattern (strategy lines 489-506).
